name_en: Tako momiuri — octopus and salt-rubbed cucumber dressed in sweet vinegar
summary_ja: 小口切りのきゅうりを塩でもみ、ゆでたこと酢で和える奈良の料理。田植えを終えて田の神に感謝する早苗饗に、大地にしっかり吸い付くタコにあやかり苗がよくつくよう願って作られてきたとされる。
summary_en: Thinly sliced cucumber rubbed with salt and dressed with boiled octopus in sweet vinegar, a Nara dish. It is said to be made for the sanaburi rite that gives thanks to the rice-field deity after planting, the octopus's suckers standing in for a wish that the seedlings take firm hold.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Nara kaki namasu — daikon and carrot in vinegar, sweetened with dried persimmon
summary_ja: 大根とニンジンの紅白なますに干し柿を加えた奈良の正月料理。砂糖が高価だった時代、干し柿の甘みで酸味をやわらげたとされ、白と赤の色は水引を意味し平安を願う縁起物として受け継がれている。
summary_en: A Nara New Year dish that adds dried persimmon to a red-and-white vinegared salad of daikon and carrot. In an age when sugar was costly, the persimmon's sweetness is said to have softened the vinegar's edge, and the red-and-white colors, echoing a ceremonial paper cord, carry a wish for peace.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
